title: Unraveling the Mechanistic Spectrum of Myhre Syndrome: SMAD4 Signaling Disruption, Skeletal Phenotypes, and Translational Innovation.
authors: Zhu, Min; Zeng, Fanyuan; Zhu, Chu
journal: American journal of medical genetics. Part C, Seminars in medical genetics
one_liner_zh: 该文综述Myhre综合征中SMAD4突变导致的信号通路与骨骼表型，虽提及AI但无蛋白质-DNA互作建模或TF-DNA结合机制研究，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Myhre syndrome (MYHRS) is an ultra-rare, progressive multisystem disorder caused by recurrent heterozygous missense variants in the SMAD4 gene, a central mediator of TGF-beta and BMP signaling. Skeletal abnormalities-including postnatal short stature, brachydactyly, thickened calvarium, and craniofacial dysmorphism-are cardinal features, often accompanied by joint contractures and progressive soft tissue fibrosis. Extensive cellular and genetic evidence supports a gain-of-function (GoF) mechanism wherein mutant SMAD4 displays increased protein stability and prolonged nuclear localization, enhancing canonical SMAD signaling and driving overexpression of profibrotic and extracellular matrix (ECM) genes. Although a dominant-negative (DN) effect was recently proposed for some variants, GoF remains the prevailing and best-supported model. The underlying skeletal pathophysiology likely reflects both primary disruption of mesenchymal differentiation affecting bone and cartilage, and secondary progressive fibrosis that amplifies contractures and skeletal rigidity over time, though direct mechanistic studies in bone tissue remain limited. Therapeutically, TGF-beta pathway inhibitors such as losartan exhibit promising in vitro and early clinical benefits, while advanced strategies-spanning targeted small molecules, anti-fibrotic agents, and emerging gene-editing approaches-are prospective direction for therapies. The integration of patient-derived iPSC models engineered animal systems, multi-modal technologies, and artificial intelligence (AI) holds significant promise for precision medicine in Myhre syndrome.
abstract_zh: Myhre综合征（MYHRS）是一种超罕见、进行性多系统疾病，由SMAD4基因中的复发性杂合错义变异引起，该基因是TGF-beta和BMP信号传导的核心介质。骨骼异常——包括出生后身材矮小、短指（趾）畸形、颅骨增厚和颅面畸形——是主要特征，通常伴有关节挛缩和进行性软组织纤维化。大量细胞和遗传学证据支持功能获得性（GoF）机制，其中突变型SMAD4表现出增加的蛋白质稳定性和延长的核定位，增强经典SMAD信号传导并驱动促纤维化和细胞外基质（ECM）基因的过度表达。尽管最近对某些变异提出了显性负性（DN）效应，但GoF仍是主流且最受支持的模型。潜在的骨骼病理生理学可能反映了影响骨和软骨的间充质分化的原发性破坏，以及随时间推移放大挛缩和骨骼僵硬的继发性进行性纤维化，尽管骨组织中的直接机制研究仍然有限。在治疗方面，TGF-beta通路抑制剂如氯沙坦在体外和早期临床中显示出有前景的益处，而先进策略——涵盖靶向小分子、抗纤维化药物和新兴基因编辑方法——是治疗的前瞻性方向。患者来源的iPSC模型、工程化动物系统、多模态技术和人工智能（AI）的整合，为Myhre综合征的精准医学带来了巨大希望。
